# dsh-file-drag
Drag files and folders from the DeepSeek Harness **Files** sidebar straight into the message compose
r. By default each dropped file becomes a small inline chip inside the sentence you are writing — th
e same rounded token the composer's own `@` picker produces — and you can switch that to an uploaded
attachment or a plain `@` path.
DeepSeek Harness already accepts file drags that come from the operating system, but its Sidebar Fil
es pane has no drag source at all, and the composer only claims drags whose payload type is `Files`.
This plugin closes that gap from the outside: it arms the existing file rows, carries the relative
path over a private MIME type, and then hands the result to the composer through its own insertion p
over a private MIME type, and then hands the result to the composer through its own insertion paths.
## Do you need this?

Watch the clip above before installing anything. The plugin only changes one thing:
it lets a file i

n the right-hand **Files** tab become something you can drop into
the middle of a sentence.

- You keep material in the workspace and refer to it by path while writing → you
will use this every

day.
- You paste code inline, or never open the Files tab → skip it. Nothing else in the
app change
s, and there is nothing to configure.
**Repository and releases:** <https://github.com/JiayuREN1127/dsh-file-drag>
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** or a build that still renders the right sidebar Files tab.
- The `
desktop` profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`), which is what the macOS app uses.

`install.sh` copies the package into `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-drag` and append
s one Loader row to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`, keeping a timestamped backup of that
row to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`, keeping a timestamped backup of that file first.
To install by hand, do the same two things:

1. Copy this package to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-drag`.
2. Append to `~/.dsh/p
rofiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`:

Then **quit the app completely (`Cmd-Q`) and reopen it**. The Loader tree is built at startup, so a
page reload is not enough for the first install. Later plugin updates only need a page reload.
## Usage

1. Open the **Files** tab in the right sidebar.
2. Press and drag a file or a folder onto the messag

e composer.
3. Release.
While dragging, the composer shows a dashed outline so you know it will accept the drop.
### Drop behaviour
Pick it in **Settings → General → File drag**:
| Mode | Result |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
**Drag source.** The Files tab renders every row as `<li data-files-entry="file|directory|other" dat
a-files-path="relative/path">`. The plugin does not guess the tree shape: on `pointerdown` it sets `
draggable` on the closest such row, so the press can turn into a drag.
**Transport.** `dragstart` writes a private payload, `application/x-dsh-file-path`, holding the rela
tive path and the entry kind. The native `Files` type is deliberately not used for the drag itself,
because a synthesized `File` has no host path and the desktop path bridge would reject it.
**Inline chip.** On drop the plugin reaches the resident composer shell for the session and calls it
s `addFiles` with one reference — the same call the composer makes when you pick a file from the `@`
menu — so the full Lexical decorator node, icon, label and clipboard projection all come from DeepS
eek Harness itself. The session-scoped `conversation` service is reached through `ctx.sessions.bindi
ng(id).ctx.get("conversation")`, because a root-level plugin cannot inject a session-scoped service.
**Attachment.** The plugin reads the file through the `workspaceFiles` client Remote (`readBytes`),
wraps the bytes in a real `File`, and replays the built-in `Files` drop onto the composer. The compo
ser then takes its own upload path, so the card behaves exactly like one dragged in from the operati
akes its own upload path, so the card behaves exactly like one dragged in from the operating system.
**@ path.** The mention is delivered as a synthetic `paste` event carrying `text/plain` on the edito
r root. The draft editor is Lexical, which ignores direct DOM writes and `document.execCommand`; a p
aste is the only reliable way in.
**Settings row.** The preference is a row registered into the `settings.general.item` slot, so it ap
pears in DeepSeek Harness's own Settings page and follows the UI language.
## Compatibility
Built against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2`. The plugin depends on implementation details that are n
ot a public contract:

- the `data-files-entry` / `data-files-path` attributes on sidebar rows,
- the composer being a `[co

ntenteditable="true"]` element that handles `paste`,
- the composer component carrying a `sessionId`

prop,
- the `settings.general.item` settings slot and the `conversation` service face,
- `window.__
ModuleLoader__.load` as the client bundle entry point.
If a future release changes any of these, the plugin degrades instead of breaking the page: every ha
ndler is guarded, a failed chip insertion falls back to the `@` path, and `apply` is wrapped so a fa
ilure never blocks boot.
## Limitations

- One item per drag; multi-select dragging is not implemented.
- Only works while the Files tab is r

endered, because the rows are the drag source.
- Drops are accepted anywhere in the window, not only

over the composer.
- Attachment mode reads files through the workspace-files Remote, so it inherits

that service's size limit; oversized files fall back to a chip.
- The mention is relative to the Fi
les tab root, which is the session workspace. A session opened in another folder still receives the
is the session workspace. A session opened in another folder still receives the same relative path.
